transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me. Um, I hope I'm doing this right. 

I guess what finally pushed me to come in is... well, my eating has just been a little all over the place lately. I'm sure it's nothing too terrible, but... some weeks I just barely touch my dinner. And then, um, other nights—and I feel a little embarrassed even admitting this—I end up just standing in the kitchen eating crackers and sweets after everyone else has gone to bed. 

I just wanted to make sure I was doing the right thing by getting it checked out. Is that... is that the sort of thing I should be bringing up?
After you eat, especially during those times you feel like you've eaten too much, do you ever make yourself vomit, take laxatives, or exercise excessively to try to balance things out?

Oh, goodness, no. Um... no, I definitely don't do anything like that. I would never want to do something so... well, drastic. 

I mostly just feel a little silly about eating the extra snacks, you know? And then I just go to bed. I promise I don't do anything to make myself sick or take any of those pills, and I'm certainly not out running miles in the middle of the night. I just try to do better the next day. 

Does that make sense? I really hope I'm answering your questions okay.
During those times when you're eating extra snacks at night, do you feel like you can't stop eating or control how much you're eating?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. Um... I definitely don't feel out of control. I mean, I could stop if I really wanted to, I just... I guess I just let myself have a little too much in the moment. 

It's really just a handful of crackers or a couple of cookies, and then I make sure to put the box away. It's not like I'm tearing through the pantry or anything scary like that. I'm fully aware of what I'm doing, it's just a bad habit I've slipped into lately. 

I really hope I'm not making a mountain out of a molehill by even bringing it up. Does that sound like a normal thing people do? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do these nighttime eating episodes cause you any distress, or have they affected your daily life in any way?

Oh, um, no, not really. I mean, it doesn't cause me any real distress or anything. I feel a tiny bit guilty sometimes, just because I know I shouldn't be snacking so late, but it hasn't changed my day-to-day life at all. 

I still get up and do everything I normally do. It's really just a minor annoyance, I suppose. I definitely don't want you to think it's ruining my life or anything dramatic like that. 

I hope it's okay that I don't have a more serious answer for you. I just want to be helpful and honest. Is it alright if it doesn't bother me that much?
Have you noticed any other changes in your eating habits or feelings around food that you think might be important to mention?

Well, um... I guess, if I'm being completely honest... and I really didn't want to make a big fuss about it, but... it is actually kind of what finally pushed me to come in and see you. My eating has just been a little... well, all over the place lately. 

Like, some weeks I barely touch my dinner at all, I just don't have much of an appetite. And then, like I was saying before, other nights I'll just stand in the kitchen eating crackers and sweets after everyone’s gone to bed. It's just a bit inconsistent, I suppose. 

I feel a little silly even mentioning it, because I know it's not the worst thing in the world and I don't want to sound like I'm complaining. Am I doing okay explaining this? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the full picture, even if it's a little embarrassing to admit that my habits have been so messy.
Have you been feeling down, depressed, or have you lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

Well, um... I guess I do have moments where I feel a little low. It's nothing too drastic, I promise. I don't want to sound like I'm whining or anything. 

It's just... sometimes I go through these stretches where the whole house just feels sort of... gray and heavy, I guess? Like, I'll just sit at the kitchen table and feel really empty inside, even if absolutely nothing bad has happened that day. It's so silly, really, because I have a lot to be thankful for. 

I try to just push through it and keep busy so I don't bother anyone with it. I hope that's a helpful answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need, even if it's a little hard to talk about. Does that sound like the kind of thing you were asking about?
Have you had days where you feel down or empty most of the time, and if so, does that happen nearly every day for a couple of weeks or more?

Well, um... I guess if I look back at everything, those... those gray periods where I just feel so empty and guilty, and I don't really want to do my normal hobbies... they do happen quite a bit. 

I really hate to admit it, because I know I should be more positive, but if I add it all up, it's probably been going on for about seven months now. Not every single second, of course! I don't want you to think I'm just miserable all the time. But, yes, it does happen most days during those stretches. 

I'm so sorry if that sounds like a lot, I really didn't mean to let it go on for so long before getting help. Am I explaining that clearly enough for your notes? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right timeline.
Have you noticed that you feel more tired or that you're lacking energy, even when you're not doing much?

Oh, um... actually, no, I don't think so. I mean, I get normal-tired at the end of the day, of course, but... I haven't really felt like I have zero energy or anything like that. 

I still manage to keep up with things around the house, so I don't want to make it sound like I'm just lying around all day doing nothing. I hope it's okay that I say no to that one? I just want to be totally honest with you, and I really haven't noticed feeling extra exhausted. Is that alright? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions the right way.
